text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The sale of state-owned Etibank for $185 million reveals that there are plenty of secret tycoons in Turkey.
- Court records show that late gangster at centre of security scandal, Abdullah Catli, often visited parliament.
- Interior minister Meral Aksener doctored list of police appointments before presenting it to president for ratification.
- A court acquits journalist Cetin Altan from charges of insulting the state in a newspaper interview.
- Large bomb defused by police at busy railway station in Istanbul.
- Pension rights to be bought at a price of $12,500.
- Group of businessmen present their democratisation plans to parliament.
- Turkey and Turkish Cypriots release declaration of "joint military action" if the Turkish side of the divided island is attcked.
